s1.syndrome_frame: Gastrointestinal bleeding in a patient with a history of cancer and cirrhosis
salient_findings: Gastrointestinal bleeding with two episodes of frank hematochezia
Severe thrombocytopenia with a platelet count of 2,000/µL
key_facts: 60-year-old man
History of squamous cell cancer of the right tongue
History of cirrhosis from hepatitis C
Platelet count 5 days before surgery was 115,000/µL
Underwent right glossectomy with bilateral neck dissection
Hepatitis C with a nucleic acid amplification test result of 1679 IU/mL
Developed gastrointestinal bleeding
Platelet count of 2,000/µL
Prothrombin time is normal
Activated partial thromboplastin time is normal
HIV status is negative
Heparin-associated antibody is negative
Bone marrow biopsy was performed
CT of the abdomen shows cirrhosis of the liver
Visceral Angiogram shows no active extravasation
Post-embolization Imaging shows approximately 60% infarction of the spleen

shortlist.label: Hypersplenism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has cirrhosis and a low platelet count, which is consistent with hypersplenism.

shortlist.label: Splenic infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Post-embolization Imaging shows approximately 60% infarction of the spleen, which could cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

shortlist.label: Portal hypertensive gastropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has cirrhosis, which can lead to portal hypertension and subsequently portal hypertensive gastropathy, a cause of gastrointestinal bleeding.

shortlist.label: Esophageal varices
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has cirrhosis, which increases the risk of developing esophageal varices, a common cause of gastrointestinal bleeding in these patients.

shortlist.label: Gastric varices
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to esophageal varices, gastric varices are also a complication of cirrhosis and portal hypertension, and could be a source of gastrointestinal bleeding.

raw.rationale: The patient's low platelet count of 2,000/µL, history of cirrhosis, and splenomegaly suggested by the 60% infarction of the spleen post-embolization are consistent with hypersplenism, which is characterized by splenic sequestration of blood cells leading to cytopenias.

rejected.label: Splenic infarction
rejected.why: Although the patient had splenic infarction, it was a result of treatment and not the primary cause of the low platelet count and other symptoms.

rejected.label: Portal hypertensive gastropathy
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence of portal hypertension causing gastropathy, and the patient's gastrointestinal bleeding could be attributed to other causes.

rejected.label: Esophageal varices
rejected.why: There is no mention of esophageal varices in the patient's diagnosis or imaging studies, making it less likely to be the primary cause of the patient's symptoms.

rejected.label: Gastric varices
rejected.why: Similar to esophageal varices, there is no mention of gastric varices, and the patient's symptoms and lab results are more consistent with hypersplenism.
